data.title: Mycobacterium w vaccine (Mw / Immuvac / MIP)
data.summary: Biologicals · Heat-killed Mycobacterium indicus pranii (formerly Mycobacterium w) — Indian immunomodulatory vaccine
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Biologicals_

**Class:** Heat-killed Mycobacterium indicus pranii (formerly Mycobacterium w) — Indian immunomodulatory vaccine

## Mechanism of action
- Shares antigens with M. leprae; boosts Th1 cell-mediated immunity and modulates cytokines
- Used as a non-specific immunostimulant

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Leprosy: adjunct to MDT in multibacillary leprosy (faster bacterial clearance, fewer reactions), immunoprophylaxis of contacts (trials)
- Off-label: recalcitrant warts (intralesional/intradermal), anogenital warts, molluscum, psoriasis, alopecia areata, vitiligo (limited data)
- Approved in India for gram-negative sepsis (adjunct)

## Dose & formulations
- Intradermal 0.1 mL (first dose may be 0.2 mL split at two sites), repeated every 2–4 weeks for warts; leprosy schedules per protocol

## Adverse effects
- Injection-site papule, ulcer, abscess and scar; fever, flu-like symptoms; lymphadenopathy

## Contraindications
- Immunosuppression; acute febrile illness; pregnancy (insufficient data)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Indian immunomodulator from M. indicus pranii — adjunct in MB leprosy and in warts

## Note on sources
Mw vaccine is described in Khopkar; Wolverton does not cover it.

_Sources: Khopkar (Immunobiologicals — Immuvac / Mw vaccine). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
